messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: High anomalous embeddings traffic from multiple API keys — detected pattern: cookie/header churn + repeated short sequences. Alerting oncall. https://redwood.internal/alerts/INC-61725 :rotating_light:
alice (sre): I'm on it, pulling kinesis + edge logs now. initial spike is primarily embeddings.async.batch POST /v1/embeddings (short seq length).
raj (oncall): taking pager. allocation looks like a fanout from a few proxy IP ranges. ETA 5.
alice (sre): metrics: 10x baseline qps to embeddings batch, token rate up, error budget dipping. Running quick check of recent deploys — none.
nina (security): suspecting scraper farm + session cookie churn. Recommend temporary WAF block on identified headers + tarpit.
oliver (eng-runtime): can we apply per-api-key hard rate cap on embeddings.batch and disable async batching while we triage? That should reduce blast radius.
emma (support): heads up — if we block keys some customers might get 429s. I'll draft a short PSA for affected customers once we know scope.
alice (sre): Actions so far:
- throttled embeddings.batch route to 5r/s per key via edge rate-slice
- disabled async batching on embeddings for all new requests (feature-flag rollback)
- pushed WAF rule to block suspicious UA and X-Forwarded-For ranges (temp)
Snippet of command used:```sh
# edge config
redwood edge rate-limit set --route embeddings.batch --per-key 5 --scope global
redwood feature-flags set embeddings.async_batching --state off --reason "mitigation-61725"
```
raj (oncall): applied tarpit (403 slow) for IP ranges 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/25, flagged 3 API keys for review.
nina (security): added signature-based WAF rule: header-fingerprint -> block + log. Will dump list to /sec/incidents/61725 after we stabilize.
oliver (eng-runtime): we're seeing request latency drop after throttle. CPU on infer nodes still elevated due to inflight KV cache churn; recommending reducing concurrency on embeddings instances by 20% to stabilize. Applying now.
alice (sre): concurrency reduced on pool embeddings-prod-1 by 20%. KV cache miss ratio decreasing.
emma (support): initial customer impact: 4 paying customers reported increased 429s; one enterprise (acct: acme-inc) hit quota freeze — CX alerted and waiting on details. Draft message: "We're throttling embeddings batch due to abusive traffic; you may see 429s — we are prioritizing production traffic and will follow up with root cause." Thoughts?
carlos (product): approve that wording. Add note: if customers need exemption, support should request emergency allowlist with justification.
raj (oncall): planning handoff at 6172509950 to night shift. Need a clear checklist for next shift: (1) WAF rule id and expiry, (2) list of flagged keys, (3) timeline of rate-limit changes, (4) customer comms draft.
alice (sre): creating incident doc and runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/61725 — adding actions and raw logs.
nina (security): follow-up: will submit a rule to IDS team to detect similar header churn patterns and propose a long-term mitigation (hardening API token binding).
emma (support): sending initial PSA to affected customers now, marking high-priority for acme-inc.
oliver (eng-runtime): leaving notes: consider re-enabling async batching in read-only mode (no new batches) once traffic normalizes, to reduce latency for legitimate small jobs.
alice (sre): summary for handoff: mitigations applied = per-key hard caps, async-batching disabled, WAF header blocks, tarpit on bad IP ranges, decreased inference concurrency. Customer impact: 429s for some batch embedding users; active CX for 1 enterprise. Next shift: continue monitoring, escalate to infra if KV cache churn resumes.
raj (oncall): noted. handing off to @sre-night. If anything spikes, page the oncall escalation. :white_check_mark:
